draft.title: First Nations knowledge of the sky
card: First Nations Australians have watched the sky for tens of thousands of years. They pass this knowledge on through stories, songs and ceremony.
They use the moon's phases, the positions of stars and signs in nature to track time. These work like a calendar.
The calendars help people predict tides, seasons and when foods are ready to gather. Different Nations have their own calendars, based on their Country.
Seasonal signs can include plants flowering, animals breeding or a change in the wind. When a sign appears, people know it is time for a task, such as gathering a food.
draft.remember: Sky and seasonal signs act as calendars that help people predict tides, seasons and foods.

a.q: Why do some First Nations Australians watch the moon, stars and seasonal signs?
opts: To predict tides, seasons and when foods are ready
To stop the seasons from changing during the year
To make the moon move faster across the night sky
To measure how far away each star is from Earth
a.why: The sky and seasonal signs work as a calendar, so people can predict tides, seasons and when foods are ready. They are used to read natural patterns, not to change them or to measure distances.
a.clue: Think of how the signs work like a calendar.

b.q: In one Nation, an elder says a certain tree flowering means a fish is ready to catch. What is the flowering being used as?
opts: A seasonal sign in a calendar
A way to change the weather
A way to measure the moon's phase
A record of how old the tree is
b.why: The flowering is a sign in nature that tells people when a food is ready. It works as part of a calendar. It does not change the weather or show the moon's phase.
b.clue: Which option is about telling the time of year?

a.best: To predict tides, seasons and when foods are ready

b.best: A seasonal sign in a calendar

problems.detail: The wrong options (stopping the seasons, making the moon move faster) are so implausible that a student can pick the right answer without knowing the idea, which makes the question too easy for Year 7.

check.summary: The facts are accurate and respectful, and both questions have one clear right answer. Question a's wrong options are too implausible to test understanding.

proposal.title: First Nations knowledge of the sky
card: First Nations Australians have watched the sky for tens of thousands of years. They pass this knowledge on through stories, songs and ceremony.
They use the moon's phases, the positions of stars and signs in nature to track time. These work like a calendar.
The calendars help people predict tides, seasons and when foods are ready to gather. Different Nations have their own calendars, based on their Country, and many have more than four seasons.

Seasonal signs can include plants flowering, animals breeding or a change in the wind. Seasons follow these signs, not fixed dates. When a sign appears, people know it is time for a task, such as gathering a food.
proposal.remember: Sky and seasonal signs act as calendars that help people predict tides, seasons and foods.

a.q: Which statement best describes how First Nations calendars work?
opts: Signs in the sky and nature mark when to do tasks
Every Nation shares the same calendar across Australia
Every year is split into four equal seasons by date
Each season starts on the same date every year
a.why: First Nations calendars are read from signs, such as the moon, stars or a plant flowering, which show when it is time for a task. They are not set by fixed dates, and different Nations have their own calendars based on their Country, often with more than four seasons.
a.clue: Does a season start on a date or when something happens?

b.q: In one Nation, an elder says a certain tree flowering means a fish is ready to catch. What is the flowering being used as?
opts: A seasonal sign in a calendar
A fixed date set for fishing
A way to measure the moon's phase
A record of how old the tree is
b.why: The flowering is a sign in nature that tells people when a food is ready, so it works as part of a calendar. It is not a fixed date, because seasons follow signs like this rather than set days, and it does not show the moon's phase.
b.clue: Which option is about telling the time of year?
